title: Elders
lead: In Israel the elders were the senior men who led families, clans and towns, judged at the city gate and spoke for the people (Exodus 3:16; Deuteronomy 21:19; Ruth 4:2). Seventy elders shared Moses's load (Numbers 11:16–17), and in Jesus's day the elders sat with the chief priests on the Jerusalem council (Mark 14:53). The first churches also had elders, Greek presbyteroi (the source of "presbyter" and "priest"), whom the New Testament also calls overseers (Acts 14:23; Acts 20:17, 28; Titus 1:5–7); churches still differ on how elders, overseers and bishops relate. In Revelation twenty-four elders sit on thrones around God (Revelation 4:4).
